Agreed success criteria include intent-classification >= 92% F1 on eval set, avg latency < 350ms for short prompts, and cost targets. Next steps: share benchmark plan, security docs, and provision baseline runs.
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-08-15 14:00 PDT
Duration: ~62 minutes
Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE), Connor Li (Redwood SE), Daniel Park (CTO, Kyphos), Lena Ortiz (ML Engineer, Kyphos), Marta Ruiz (Product, Kyphos)

[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Maya from Redwood, AE on this account, and we also have Connor our SE who will dig into the technical bits. How's everyone doing?
[00:10] Daniel: Good, thanks. Busy week but excited to get this scoped.
[00:18] Lena: Hi all. We want to make sure we cover the model tradeoffs — accuracy, latency, and cost — and the multilingual requirement up front.
[00:28] Connor: Awesome. Quick agenda: confirm success criteria, go through workload sizing, discuss benchmark plan and timelines, then propose an open-model shortlist and tradeoffs. Sound good?
[00:36] Marta: Yes. Also we need to confirm SSO and data residency expectations.

[02:05] Maya: Cool. Daniel, can you give us a one-paragraph on the primary POC use-case?
[02:12] Daniel: Sure. We're building a multilingual customer support assistant to triage tickets and draft suggested replies. Primarily English and Spanish, some Portuguese and French. Volume-wise we expect 150k messages/month initially, spike to 300k with peak campaigns. Latency target is sub-350ms for short templates, but we can tolerate up to 700ms for longer generations. Accuracy — we want intent classification / routing at >= 92% F1 and suggested reply quality judged by a small human eval to be within 1.5 points of our internal baseline.

[04:40] Connor: Good detail. For that workload sizing, can you confirm average tokens per request and batch expectations?
[04:48] Lena: Average user prompt is ~30 tokens, replies range 40–120 tokens. Typical pattern is single-turn triage, sometimes a follow-up. Concurrency during peaks maybe 60–80 qps. Batch sizing: we'd prefer low latency so small batch, 1–8.

[06:20] Connor: Ok that helps. For POC we recommend two benchmark profiles: 1) short-latency path: avg 40 tokens total, 8–80 qps, single-turn; 2) long-generation path: avg 160 tokens, lower qps. We'll run both to evaluate latency and cost.

[07:50] Marta: What about multilingual quality? We care more about Spanish parity with English, Portuguese/French lower priority.
[07:58] Maya: Noted. We'll include multilingual eval sets weighted 60% English, 30% Spanish, 10% other.

[09:30] Connor: Now model shortlist. Because you asked open-models, our initial shortlist is: Llama-3 (7B and 13B variants), Mistral-Instruct, Phi-3-lite, and some TGI-quantized 13B variants (we'll call out 8-bit and 4-bit profiles). Pros/cons: Llama-3 tends to be strong on instruction-following and developer tooling; Mistral has good throughput and cost per token; Phi-3-lite shows promise for multilingual; quantized variants give big cost wins but may reduce quality on rare-language prompts.
[10:45] Daniel: We use a domain-specific taxonomy for intents; will open models handle that without fine-tuning?
[10:55] Connor: For intent classification, you can do few-shot or prompt engineering, but for top-tier recall in narrow taxonomy you'll probably want to eval both prompting and a small supervised finetune or adapter. For the POC we can test prompt-only first and a 1–3 epoch LoRA as a second axis. We'll include that in the plan.

[13:20] Lena: Can you quantify expected latency/cost differences? Even ballpark numbers per 1k requests?
[13:28] Connor: Ballpark: for a 7B quantized on GPU you might see 5–15ms per token kernel time, which translates to maybe $0.40–$1.20 per 1k short requests in hosted pricing; 13B models 1.5–2x that. Dedicated pools change the math — reserved throughput can bring cost-per-inference down substantially. We'll include a cost model spreadsheet.

[15:10] Marta: Any gotchas with KV caches or prefix caching for this workload? We have many repeated prefixes (greetings, system prompts).
[15:18] Connor: That's a place Redwood shines — prefix/KV caching can reduce token compute by ~20–40% depending on repetition. We'll instrument the baseline to measure hit rates. Note: caching behavior differs with quantization and model architecture; we'll call that out in results.

[18:00] Daniel: Security — we need SOC 2 type II, SSO (SAML), and customer-managed KMS. Are those available?
[18:08] Maya: Yes, Redwood supports SOC 2, SAML SSO, and integrations with major KMS/HSM providers. We'll share the security packet. For Private/VPC deployments we can support customer-managed keys and audit logs.

[20:35] Lena: For the POC data, can we redact PII? We will provide synthetic-ish samples but want to ensure retention policies.
[20:44] Maya: Absolutely. We'll run on non-prod environment and follow retention rules. We'll include retention config in the SOW.

[22:10] Connor: Benchmark specifics: we'll run representative synthetic trace (30k samples) and a separate human-eval set (200 examples) for quality scoring. Metrics: latency p50/p90, throughput, cost per 1k requests, F1/accuracy for intent, human preference for replies. Does that align?
[22:30] Daniel: Yes. The 200 example human eval will be our decision gate for quality.

[25:05] Marta: Timeline? We need a pilot in ~5 weeks.
[25:12] Maya: Proposed timeline: share scope and security docs this week, provision baseline Dedicated trial in 1–2 weeks, run benchmarks and LoRA trials week of 8/24, deliver results and recommendation by 9/3. That hits ~3 weeks for active runs plus reporting.

[27:40] Connor: On model selection tradeoffs: if you want strict parity English->Spanish, we may prioritize models with strong multilingual embeddings or incorporate translation+monolingual model approach. Phi-3-lite showed good Spanish tokens in our internal runs, but we should validate on your taxonomy.

[29:55] Lena: For the LoRA/fine-tune budget — what's reasonable?
[30:02] Connor: For a 7B model, a few-epoch LoRA on ~10k examples is modest compute — can run on a single GPU in hours. For 13B multiply accordingly. We'll include cost estimates for training.

[33:15] Daniel: Any concerns about hallucination for suggested replies? Our support is sensitive about suggesting wrong actions.
[33:25] Connor: Good point. We'll add a risk metric and guard rails: explicit grounding, confidence threshold, and produce classification + suggested reply with citations/backoff to agents. We can also test a conservative decode setting.

[36:40] Marta: Can you share previous benchmarks or reference links?
[36:46] Maya: We'll send the public benchmark spreadsheet and a sample Redwood-run report. (Link placeholder) See: https://app.redwood.ai/pocs/kyphos-bench-templates and security packet at https://redwood.ai/security/pk.

[38:20] Lena: For the baseline runs, what infra will you provision? GPU type?
[38:28] Connor: We'll start with an A100/Host that matches your region for fair comparison; for Dedicated-like runs we can replicate the same GPU family, and for quantized 4-bit we can also test on cheaper GPUs to show cost deltas. We'll document the exact kernel/compilation choices (e.g., fused attention vs mem-optimized) in the run sheet — sometimes the transcript of our runtime picks shows up as "kernel: fmha_v2" or similar.

[41:05] Daniel: Are there any licensing or model use constraints we should be aware of for the open models?
[41:12] Maya: We'll call out model licenses per candidate. Some community models have use restrictions; we always flag that. For production it's usually fine but must check each model's license.

[43:30] Connor: Quick note on metrics collection: we'll provide token-level cost, per-request latency, and per-route dashboards in Redwood Console so you'll see where cost is coming from.

[45:50] Marta: If the POC goes well, what's next? Full pilot or Dedicated contract?
[45:58] Maya: We typically move to a dedicated pilot with committed throughput. We'll provide pricing scenarios for hosted vs dedicated.

[48:12] Lena: Anything else we should prepare?
[48:18] Connor: Provide datasets (even synthetic), taxonomy, success thresholds, and a contact for infra/networking so we can wire SSO/KMS if needed.

[50:45] Maya: Quick recap / action items: we (Redwood) will send POC scope doc, benchmark plan, security packet, and pricing by Wed 8/18; Connor will draft benchmark config and LoRA plan by 8/20; Kyphos (Lena) will upload sample data and success criteria by 8/17. We'll provision trial infra and aim to run baselines week of 8/24.

[52:10] Daniel: Sounds good. One small question — for the multilingual path, would you recommend translation + English model or native multilingual?
[52:22] Connor: Short answer: test both. Often translation to English with high-quality MT plus a strong English model gives consistent behavior, but end-to-end multilingual models can be more efficient and avoid translation artifacts. We'll include both in the bench matrix.

[55:00] Marta: Ok, let's wrap. Thanks all.
[55:07] Maya: Thanks everyone — we'll follow up with the docs.
[55:12] Daniel: Appreciate it.

Notes: There is occasional filler and mis-attrs in transcription. Phrases like "Redwood Dedicate" (sic) and "K-V cache" appear. References shared: https://app.redwood.ai/pocs/kyphos-bench-templates, security packet link noted.

End of transcript.
